Initial indications are that such an arrangement will not block the navigation channel as the overall channel is more than 500 feet wide from the northern bank of the T-RICH site to the marine berths on the northern side of the channel. If the cargo deck barge is an industry-standard 72 feet wide, and the pontoon barge is approximately 50 feet wide, that leaves 378 feet of clearance to the berths on the other side of the channel for ships to pass through. The largest ships that would be expected to transit this particular shipping channel would be “Panamax” ships with a beam not exceeding 105.6 feet. This is believed to be an acceptable arrangement. Fabrication will be conducted generally from West to East and South to North such that the first equipment sited does not interfere with subsequent deliveries. It is therefore essential that the procurement priorities are aligned with the fabrication sequence. First to be constructed will be the administration building / workshop. This can be used initially as support offices and workforce facilities, before being changed over to offices and control buildings providing for a 'one' build option in the schedule. Storage tanks can then be installed on their foundations in sequence and progressively tied into the piping and control networks. Liquefaction trains and metering facilities can be installed as they are delivered with the westerly train installed first. It is recommended that as far as practical large pre-assembled units (PAUs) be used to minimize the need for site fabrication and integration. The vent stack is likely to be pre-fabricated in multiple sections and erected on site using mobile cranes. Page98 of158
